sentences.text: 2. Brief facts as stated are that an accident occurred on 13.05.2007, when driver of Maxi Cab bearing registration no.KA-22/2649 in which Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani was traveling, drove it in rash and negligent manner leading to accident.
In said accident, Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.
3. Claiming compensation for same, he filed claim petition in MVC.no.1912/2007 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, against owner and insurer of Maxi Cab.
4. On service of summons, owner did not appear.
He was placed ex-parte.
Only insurer filed objections denying age, occupation and income of claimant as well as injuries and disability sustained.
Issuance of insurance policy was denied.
5. During pendency of claim petition, on 10.10.2007, Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani fell down while riding bicycle and sustained injury to his abdomen.
Said injury led to death on 13.12.2007.

Alleging that death of Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani was due to injuries sustained in earlier accident aggravated by subsequent fall, his mother was impleaded as claimant and nature of claim was changed from that of personal injury claim to one of loss of dependency.
It was alleged that since death was due to aggravation of injuries sustained in earlier accident, while Manjunath Girajimani was under treatment, insurer was liable to pay compensation.
6. In said accident, there was death of another inmate of Maxi Cab and separate claim petition was filed.
Both claim petitions were clubbed together.

7. Thereafter, tribunal framed issues, recorded evidence of claimant wherein claimants were examined as PW-1 and PW-2, Dr. S.S.Karlatti, Dr. R.B.Patil and Sri. 8.
On consideration, tribunal held that accident occurred on 13.05.2007 due to rash and negligent driving of Maxi Cab by its driver and said Maxi Cab was insured with insurer.
But, tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.30,000/- towards medical expenses.
Not satisfied with quantum of compensation this appeal is filed for enhancement.

9. Sri. Sanjay S. Katageri, learned counsel for claimant-appellant submitted that first accident occurred on 13.05.2007 for which he was indoor patient for one month and underwent laprotomy on 22.08.2007.
Thereafter, claimant was under treatment of several doctors as out-door patient.
During such period, while he was riding bicycle, he fell down and sustained injuries to his abdomen area and died.

Though, subsequent fall from bicycle caused injuries, death was due to aggravation of earlier injuries and therefore death had to be presumed as due to accidental injuries and compensation assessed as such.
10. It was submitted that PW-4-Dr. Ravi B. Patil, who had treated Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani stated that death was possible as result of injuries sustained in accident.
Therefore, tribunal was not justified in denying just compensation.
11. On other hand, Sri N.R. Kuppelur, learned counsel for insurer submitted that after in-patient treatment, claimant was discharged from Vijaya Hospital, Belgaum after he had recovered fully.
Fact that subsequent fall occurred while Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani was riding bicycle would also indicate recovery.
Therefore, injuries sustained due to fall from bicycle cannot be related to injuries sustained in earlier accident.
Hence, insurer would not be liable as same was not due to use of motor vehicle.

12. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
13.

From above submission, occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle leading to Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani sustaining injuries due to rash and negligent driving by driver of insured vehicle is not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani sustained injuries on his abdominal region due to fall from bicycle subsequently and died some time thereafter.

While it is case of claimant that Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani had not recovered fully from injuries sustained in earlier accident and subsequent injuries aggravated earlier therefore,
insurer would be liable to pay compensation; it is case of insurer that Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani was discharged from hospital after full recovery and there was no relation between death and earlier injuries.
Hence, insurer was not liable to pay compensation.

sentences.text: Tribunal assessed compensation towards medical expenses and loss of estate only.
Insurer is not in appeal.
Only claimant has filed appeal for enhancement.

Therefore, point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
15. In order to establish that death was due to accidental injuries, claimant - mother of deceased was examined as PW-2 and Dr.Ravi Patil as PW-4.
PW-2 stated that even after discharge from Vijaya Hospital, Belgaum, Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani had not recovered fully.
While under treatment, he fell down from bicycle and died after sustaining further injuries.
Though PW-4 - Dr. Ravi Patil also stated that death was possible due to injuries sustained, he stated that Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani had last visited him for treatment on 10.10.2007.
In his cross-examination he denied suggestions that death was not due to accidental injuries but due to some other reason.
16. However, PW-4 admitted that after 10.10.2007, he had not seen/treated Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani.
Such being case, PW-4 would be incompetent to depose about cause of death which occurred on 13.12.2007.
Therefore, presumption that discharge was after complete recovery has to be drawn.
And for lack of adequate evidence, it has to be held that there was no causal connection between death and accidental injuries.
Consequently, insurer would not be liable to pay compensation towards loss of dependency.

But, it is settled law that even where injured - 10 - claimant died during pendency of claim petition and death was not due to accidental injuries,
compensation towards pecuniary loss to estate has to be granted.

17. Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/- towards medical expenses though medical bills for Rs.1,80,000/- were produced, by observing that they were in respect of treatment for injuries sustained after fall from bicycle.
On careful perusal of records, it is found that claimant would be entitled for another sum of Rs.13,000/- towards medical expenses for treatment taken prior to 10.10.2007.
Taking same into account, award towards medical expenses is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
18. Apart from above compensation, mother of Manjunath Adiveppa Girajimani would have loss earning during period of treatment.
She would also - 11 - be required to be compensated towards money spent on incidental expenses.

If sum of Rs.30,000/-
is awarded towards same, it would be appropriate.

Thus, total reassessed compensation would be as follows:
